entries.short_description: Benefit payments from the Old-Age and Survivors Insurance and Disability Insurance trust funds.
entries.description: Covers the federal Old-Age and Survivors Insurance and Disability Insurance trust funds, along with general-fund subsidies of those funds. At $1,580.7 billion in FY2025, it was the largest single category of federal spending.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 650 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:613-615), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $1,580.7B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Interest the government pays on money it has borrowed.
entries.description: Interest paid on the public debt — the ongoing cost of past borrowing — plus interest on uninvested funds and tax refunds, partly offset by interest the government itself collects. The $1,215.6 billion shown here is interest paid before those offsets; the offsets appear as negative '(offsetting)' line items.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 900 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:790-804), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 displayed outlays $1,215.6B (treasury.budget_categories; official net interest in federal_annual_summary).

entries.short_description: The federal Medicare health-insurance trust funds.
entries.description: Covers federal hospital insurance and federal supplementary medical insurance — Medicare's two trust funds — along with general-fund subsidies of those funds. FY2025 outlays were $996.7 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 570 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:533-537), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $996.7B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Federal health programs other than Medicare, including medical services, research, and safety inspection.
entries.description: Programs whose basic purpose is to promote physical and mental health, including preventing illness and accidents — Medicare is counted separately by law. Includes medical services for individuals and families financed through grants, contracts, insurance, or reimbursements; health research and training; and consumer and occupational safety work such as food and drug inspection. FY2025 outlays were $978.5 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 550 + subfunctions 551/552/554 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:495-531), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $978.5B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: The common defense and security of the United States.
entries.description: Raising, equipping, and maintaining the armed forces (including civilian support); developing and using weapons systems, including nuclear weapons; pay and benefits for active military and civilian personnel; defense research, development, testing, and evaluation; and procurement, construction, and stockpiling for national security. Veterans' benefits are counted separately. FY2025 outlays were $916.1 billion. A note on auditability: per GAO's audit report in the FY 2025 Financial Report of the U.S. Government, the Department of Defense received disclaimers of opinion on its fiscal years 2025 and 2024 financial statements — its internal accounting could not be verified by auditors.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 050 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:25-60), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $916.1B (treasury.budget_categories); audit sentence from GAO Independent Auditor's Report, FY2025 Financial Report of the U.S. Government p.211 (fiscal.treasury.gov, fetched 2026-06-12).

entries.short_description: Support payments to people, including unemployment, food, and housing assistance.
entries.description: Support payments to persons — retirement, disability, unemployment, and welfare programs other than Social Security and veterans' programs. Includes food and nutrition programs such as Food Stamps and Child Nutrition, unemployment and workers' compensation, public assistance cash payments, and low- and moderate-income housing benefits. FY2025 outlays were $701.6 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 600 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:545-562), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $701.6B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Benefits and services for veterans, their dependents, and survivors.
entries.description: Programs whose eligibility is tied to prior military service: veterans' compensation, life insurance, pensions, and burial benefits; G.I. Bill education and rehabilitation; hospital and medical care financed by the Department of Veterans Affairs; and housing loan programs. FY2025 outlays were $377.2 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 700 + subfunctions 701-705 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:623-675), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $377.2B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Roads, rail, transit, aviation, and water transportation.
entries.description: Provides for transportation of the public and its property: construction of facilities, equipment purchases, research and testing, communications like air traffic control, operating subsidies for facilities such as airports and industries such as railroads, and transportation-specific regulation. Covers ground transportation (roads, highways, railroads, urban mass transit), air, and water. FY2025 outlays were $145.3 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 400 + subfunctions 401-403 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:323-397), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $145.3B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.name_key: education, training, employment, and social services
entries.short_description: Education programs, job training, and social services.
entries.description: Promotes the extension of knowledge and skills, employment opportunities, workplace standards, and services to the needy: preschool through vocational education, college and graduate programs, education research and aids for the arts and libraries, job and skill training and placement, and social services such as vocational rehabilitation. FY2025 outlays were $107.0 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 500 + subfunctions 501-506 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:440-499), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $107.0B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Managing public lands, water, parks, and pollution control.
entries.description: Developing, managing, and maintaining the nation's natural resources and environment: water protection, conservation, and irrigation; the public domain and national forests; recreational lands including fish, wildlife, and parks; historic preservation; and controlling air, water, and land pollution. FY2025 outlays were $89.8 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 300 + subfunctions 301-306 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:195-247), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $89.8B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Federal law enforcement, courts, prisons, and justice grants.
entries.description: Judicial services, police protection, and law enforcement, including civil rights: operating the FBI, Customs and Border Protection, Immigration and Customs Enforcement, and the Drug Enforcement Administration; the courts and federal prosecution and defense; incarceration, parole, and rehabilitation of federal prisoners; and grants helping state and local governments improve their justice systems. FY2025 outlays were $83.1 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 750 + subfunctions 751-754 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:677-716), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $83.1B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Community economic development and disaster recovery.
entries.description: Develops physical facilities and financial infrastructure to promote viable community economies: community development block grants for largely urban areas, economic development aid for depressed and rural regions, and helping communities and families recover from natural disasters. FY2025 outlays were $82.4 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 450 + subfunctions 451-453 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:405-438), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $82.4B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Diplomacy, foreign aid, and international security assistance.
entries.description: Maintains peaceful relations, commerce, and travel between the United States and the rest of the world and promotes international security and economic development abroad: humanitarian and development assistance, security assistance to foreign governments, diplomatic and consular operations of the State Department, cultural exchanges, and international financial programs. FY2025 outlays were $60.1 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 150 + subfunctions 151-155 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:80-134), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $60.1B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Farm income stabilization and agricultural research.
entries.description: Promotes the economic stability of agriculture and the nation's capability to maintain and increase agricultural production: subsidies and payments to stabilize farm prices, agricultural commodity stockpiles, farm price support loans, and agricultural research and extension services. FY2025 outlays were $47.4 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 350 + subfunctions 351-352 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:227-273), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $47.4B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Business and housing-credit programs, economic data, and the Postal Service fund.
entries.description: Promotion and regulation of commerce and the housing credit and deposit insurance industries: collecting and publishing social and economic data such as the census, general-purpose subsidies to businesses including housing credit, mortgage and homeownership loan programs, deposit insurance protecting bank deposits, small business loans, and the Postal Service fund. FY2025 outlays were $44.7 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 370 + subfunctions 371-376 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:275-331), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $44.7B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Central overhead: Congress, the White House, tax collection, and property management.
entries.description: The general overhead of the federal government: legislative and executive branch operations, tax collection and fiscal operations of the Treasury, property and records management, central personnel management, and general fiscal assistance to state, local, and territorial governments. FY2025 outlays were $43.1 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 800 + subfunctions 801-806 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:694-776), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $43.1B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Basic science research and the space program.
entries.description: Science and research activities of the federal government that aren't part of another function: National Science Foundation research, all NASA space programs — space transportation, space science, and new technologies for future missions — and general science research supported by the Department of Energy. FY2025 outlays were $42.0 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 250 + subfunctions 251-252 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:136-165), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $42.0B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Energy supply, conservation, and emergency reserves.
entries.description: Promotes an adequate supply and appropriate use of energy to serve the needs of the economy: developing domestic energy resources and supply systems, encouraging prudent use of energy, maintaining an emergency petroleum stockpile, and energy information and regulation. Defense-related atomic energy work is counted under National Defense. FY2025 outlays were $20.8 billion.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: GAO-05-734SP App. IV, function 270 + subfunctions 271-276 (docs/federal/gao_appendix4.txt:161-203), fetched 2026-06-12; sourced figure: FY2025 outlays $20.8B (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.name_key: department of health and human services
entries.short_description: The department running federal health and human-services programs, dominated by Medicare and Medicaid spending.
entries.description: HHS's stated mission is "to enhance and protect the health and well-being of all Americans" through health and human services and advances in medicine, public health, and social services. In FY2025 it was the largest-spending federal department at $2,671.5 billion (gross of offsets), led by the Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services ($2,485.0B) and the Administration for Children and Families ($75.7B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/075/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: The agency that runs Social Security's retirement and disability trust funds.
entries.description: SSA's stated mission is to "deliver Social Security services that meet the changing needs of the public." Its FY2025 spending of $1,710.4 billion flows almost entirely through two trust funds: Old-Age and Survivors Insurance ($1,420.8B) and Disability Insurance ($160.2B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/028/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Manages the government's finances — including paying interest on the debt and running the IRS.
entries.description: Treasury's stated mission includes maintaining a strong economy, protecting the integrity of the financial system, and managing the U.S. Government's finances and resources. Most of its $1,539.7 billion in FY2025 spending is Interest on the Public Debt ($1,215.6B), followed by the Internal Revenue Service ($291.0B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/020/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: The military forces of the United States.
entries.description: The Department of Defense's stated mission is "to provide the military forces needed to deter war and to protect the security of our country." Its FY2025 military-programs spending of $870.9 billion was led by Operation and Maintenance ($342.4B) and Military Personnel ($206.5B). A note on auditability: per GAO's audit report in the FY 2025 Financial Report of the U.S. Government, DoD received disclaimers of opinion on its fiscal years 2025 and 2024 financial statements — its internal accounting could not be verified by auditors.
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/097/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories); audit sentence from GAO Independent Auditor's Report, FY2025 Financial Report of the U.S. Government p.211 (fiscal.treasury.gov, fetched 2026-06-12).

entries.short_description: Serves America's veterans with benefits and health care.
entries.description: VA's stated mission is to fulfill President Lincoln's promise "to care for him who shall have borne the battle, and for his widow, and his orphan" by serving and honoring America's veterans. Its $386.9 billion in FY2025 spending was led by Benefits Programs ($223.8B) and the Veterans Health Administration ($118.5B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/036/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Food, farming, rural development, and nutrition programs.
entries.description: USDA's stated mission is to provide leadership on food, agriculture, natural resources, rural development, and nutrition. The largest share of its $231.1 billion in FY2025 spending was the Food and Nutrition Service ($148.3B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/012/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: The federal workforce agency — most of its spending is federal employee retirement.
entries.description: OPM's stated mission is to "recruit, retain, and honor a world-class workforce to serve the American people." Most of its $183.5 billion in FY2025 spending flows through the Civil Service Retirement and Disability Fund ($110.2B plus a $51.6B general-fund payment into the fund).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/024/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Federal education programs — led by student aid.
entries.description: The Department of Education's stated mission is to promote student achievement and preparation for global competitiveness by fostering educational excellence and ensuring equal access. Its $187.9 billion in FY2025 spending was led by the Office of Federal Student Aid ($111.3B) and the Office of Elementary and Secondary Education ($43.4B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/091/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).

entries.short_description: Safeguarding the American people and homeland — led by FEMA and border protection.
entries.description: DHS's stated mission is to "safeguard the American people, our homeland, and our values." Its $133.3 billion in FY2025 spending was led by the Federal Emergency Management Agency ($62.6B) and U.S. Customs and Border Protection ($21.2B).
entries.evidence_summary: Authored inline from: USAspending /api/v2/agency/070/ official mission (fetched 2026-06-12); sourced figures: FY2025 agency-lens outlays (treasury.budget_categories).
